items.q: What are the classic indicators that we’re in an AI bubble?
items.a: Great bubbles form around **real transformative ideas** (railroads, internet, AI) when capital over-invests. Grantham flags **pure crazy euphoria** signals like SpaceX narratives claiming a quarter of global GDP as addressable market — timing that can mean the peak is near.

items.q: If AI is real, why still sell?
items.a: Because **bubble ≠ scam**. The idea can reshape the world while high-flyers still suffer **70%+ drawdowns**; Nasdaq fell ~82% in 2000 before winners later inherited the spoils.

items.q: What simple portfolio stance does Grantham recommend?
items.a: **Don’t own US stocks** as the default. Prefer ~**60% non-US / EM equities**, some bonds and cash, **5–10% precious metals**, and skip crypto (he expects it to go to zero).

items.q: Why won’t your advisor tell you to get out?
items.a: **Career risk in bull markets** — underperform while the party continues and clients fire you. Sell-side marketing stayed bullish in 1999 even when the engine room privately agreed a bear market was coming.

items.q: How extreme is US inequality in Grantham’s framing?
items.a: US **Gini** is now Brazil/Mexico tier after post-1975 stagnation for median hours worked. History rarely fixes extremes via peaceful policy — resets come via **war, revolution, or collapse**.

items.q: Is housing still a safe wealth engine?
items.a: Even a **30% drop** can leave homes expensive vs incomes. **Population decline** plus unaffordable prices means fewer future bidders, not automatic appreciation.

items.q: What fertility data does he treat as an emergency?
items.a: Sperm counts ~**100M/mL in 1970 → ~35 today**, declining ~2.5%/year. Endocrine disruptors (phthalates, BPA, PFAS, microplastics) and pesticide exposure are the suspects.

items.q: Why does he prefer EU-style chemical rules?
items.a: EU banned ~**1,500 cosmetic chemicals** vs ~**12 in the US**; ~85 pesticides legal in the US are banned in the EU. Highest leverage: pregnant women going organic on dirty-dozen produce and skipping cosmetics.
